chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from some of his companions, from Ahmad ibn Qutaybah al-Hamdani, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said:

I said to Abī 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him): On the night of 'Arafah, I was in Ḥā`ir praying. I saw close to fifty thousand handsome men who smelled beautiful and who were praying Salāt all night. It was after dawn that I prostrated and when I raised my head, I could not see any of them. Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: Fifty thousand angels passed by Ḥusain (peace be upon him) while he was being killed so they ascended to the heavens. Allāh, the Exalted, revealed to them, 'You passed by the son of My love and he was being killed but you did not help him. Descend to the earth and dwell near his grave while you are disheveled and covered with dust until the rising of the Hour.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the fifty thousand angels passing by Imam Husain (a.s.) during his martyration?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarah* highlights the cosmic significance of Karbala by linking the earthly martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with the celestial realm, where fifty thousand angels witnessed the event but were held accountable for their lack of intervention. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elucidates that these angels were commanded to descend and reside near his grave until the Day of Resurrection, establishing a perpetual spiritual connection between the heavens and the shrine of the Imam. This underscores the Shia belief in the ongoing intercession and presence of divine beings at the graves of the Ahl al-Bayt.
